_comment: EXT-17 committed example conditions for the Atacama Air Defense scenario (CR-AS-3,
CR-PAR-2, CR-DOC-2).
The shape is EXT-08's, adopted verbatim at M6 - OQ-5, decided by writing these seven
conditions in the vendored shape and evaluating them against the seven committed
captures rather than by reading the schema, which is how the one added key was found.
THREE RULES DIFFER FROM THE VENDORED DOCUMENT, each for a reason this project measured:
1. An unknown key and a key written twice are REFUSED by name, not ignored. The
capture format's ignore-unknown rule (s13) is right for a capture and wrong for a
file a person writes - F-23 measured a campaign file silently accepting "value"
for "values". A key beginning with '_' is a comment, which is what this is.
2. A verdict is THREE-valued: met, not_met, indeterminate. The vendored met:false at
end of run is a conclusion drawn from absence, which CR-AS-4 forbids.
3. "scenario_unload" is refused as a removal_reason. It is the removal the engine's
stop path writes for every surviving entity at teardown - 267 of 385 removals
across the committed sweep, all at sim_time_s 0 - so a condition on it is met in
every run for every entity.
ONE KEY IS ADDED: "expect", taking "met" (the default) or "not_met". The vendored
schema is a referee - it reports whether a condition was satisfied and says nothing about
whether that is good news. EXT-17 must map those facts onto CR-EX-5's four run outcomes,
and two of the brief's three questions survive that reading while the third does not:
"did anything reach a terminal state it SHOULD NOT have" is an assertion of
non-occurrence, and the vendored shape can express one only for the area kind through
test: inside|outside. Without expect, command-centre-destroyed asserts that the command
centre SHOULD be destroyed - the inverse of the question. The verdict still records the
fact in the vendored schema's own terms; expect is a separate field and a separate
question, so EXT-08's verdicts and EXT-17's stay directly comparable.
Units are the platform's own and are never converted: metres for distances, degrees for
angles, and geodetic positions in the platform's [lat, lon, alt] order (format v1 s15).
Distances are straight-line on WGS-84 ECEF - see src/assert/Geodesy.h, which states the
constants so any verdict here is reproducible with a calculator (CR-AS-2).
THE SWEEP FLIP (CR-PAR-2's third criterion). Measured across the committed sweep:
closest approach falls 8693.17 m at 11 m/s to 2934.45 m at 165 and 220, so this
condition is NOT MET at 11/27.5/55/82.5/110 and MET at 165/220. Every not-met
verdict is sound rather than indeterminate - the tightest margin, 711.87 m at
110 m/s, clears its 11.00 m continuity bound by a factor of 65.
A SECOND FLIP, at a different value, and of a different kind - the corridor is
entered from 110 m/s upward where the proximity threshold is only reached from 165.
Two conditions flipping at two thresholds is a trend rather than one binary.
The circle form of the area kind, exercised distinctly. The vendored example centres
its circle on the airfield's own position with the same 3000 m radius, which makes it
arithmetically identical to the proximity condition above - the airfield never moves,
so the two agree in all seven runs to the centimetre. A wider ring around the ammo
depot tests the same kind and answers a different question.
The terminal_state kind in its removal_reason form, and a NEVER-MET case - asserted
that way with expect: not_met, because the raid leader surviving is the outcome this
condition is checking for. The verdict is a sound not_met rather than indeterminate,
because every occupancy of it is accounted for - format v1 s8.1 makes a sample at the
segment's last instant positive evidence of non-removal.
The brief's own dangerous question - 'did anything reach a terminal state it SHOULD
NOT have' - asked of the asset it matters most for, and the condition that could not
be written at all without expect. Never met in any committed run, and soundly so.
The field+equals form, MET in every run at sim_time_s 0.05. A met verdict is always
sound: it is computed from a record that is present.
CR-AS-4's INDETERMINATE, demonstrated rather than described - and it is a genuine
case rather than a contrived one. RedUAV_N_01 carries health 'nominal' in all 1196
of its samples in every committed run. A naive referee would report this NOT MET,
confidently, from a file in which the frame it happened in may simply be missing.
Nothing in the capture format bounds how fast a string field may change, so the
value could have been taken and left inside one 0.1 s sampling gap. This form is
never decidable in the negative, and the honest answer is that the capture cannot say.
Note what expect does NOT do here: asserting not_met does not make an indeterminate
verdict satisfied. An undetermined outcome is neither, which is CR-AS-4's whole point.
